subject: 95% CI for std.all based on imputed data

messages.author: fdc70beaef2da0e2
messages.subject: 95% CI for std.all based on imputed data
parts:
Hi all, good morning! 

I am trying to obtain 95% CI's for my std.all's, based on imputed data. 
I am running the below R code, however this returns the CI's for the unstandardized coefficients. 

myfit_model1.3 <- runMI(Model1.3_atthe, data = imp, fun = "sem", estimator = "WLSMV", std.lv = T, m = 30, miPackage = "mice", seed = 2000)

summary(myfit_model1.3, standardized=T, rsq=T, ci = TRUE)

Is there anyway to retrieve the 95% CI's for the std.all's based on imputed data? Any idea how I could get the CIs of the standardized coefficients? 

All suggestions are welcome! Thanks in advance.

Best,

Joost

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: 95% CI for std.all based on imputed data
parts:
On 7/27/20 11:35 AM, Joost G wrote:
> I am trying to obtain 95% CI's for my std.all's, based on imputed data.
> I am running the below R code, however this returns the CI's for the
> unstandardized coefficients.
>

> /myfit_model1.3 <- runMI(Model1.3_atthe, data = imp, fun = "sem",
> estimator = "WLSMV", std.lv = T, m = 30, miPackage = "mice", seed = 2000)/
>
> /summary(myfit_model1.3, standardized=T, rsq=T, ci = TRUE)/

>
> Is there anyway to retrieve the 95% CI's for the std.all's based on
> imputed data?

Hm. The 'usual' way is by using standardizedSolution(). But this does
not work for runMI objects.

If your model is scale-invariant, you may get close by using both std.lv
= TRUE (which you already do) and std.ov = TRUE.

Yves.
